summary: McArthur River Mine Airport (MCV/YMHU) is a remote airstrip in Australia's Northern Territory, serving the massive McArthur River zinc and lead mine—one of the world's largest zinc operations. The airport primarily handles fly-in fly-out (FIFO) workers and occasional charter flights, operating as a vital lifeline to one of the most isolated industrial sites in the country. Surrounded by rugged Gulf Country terrain, it functions almost exclusively as a workforce transport hub rather than a passenger destination.
faqs:
Q: Who typically uses McArthur River Mine Airport?
A: The airport is used almost exclusively by fly-in fly-out (FIFO) mine workers, visiting contractors, and occasional charter passengers connected to the McArthur River zinc-lead mine operations.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights to MCV?
A: No scheduled commercial passenger service operates to MCV. All flights are charter or company-arranged services linked to the mine.

Q: What facilities are available at the terminal?
A: The terminal offers basic amenities suited to a mining workforce, including a small waiting area and check-in counters. It is not equipped for general tourism use.

Q: Can tourists visit the McArthur River Mine?
A: Public access to the mine is restricted due to safety and operational requirements. Visitors must have prior approval and arrangement with the mining operator.
transport_tips: Access to the airport is by mine-arranged transport only, as there are no public buses or taxis serving the remote site. Most travelers arrive via charter flights from Darwin or other Northern Territory hubs. Ground transport from the airstrip to the mine camp is typically provided by the operating company for authorized personnel.
local_tip: Workers on roster should pack light and confirm baggage allowances in advance, as the small apron limits aircraft size and sometimes results in tight weight restrictions. Bringing your own snacks for the remote camp is also recommended, as on-site supplies can be limited.
